project.description:
ZFIN-10486: Weekly read-only report. Compares each feature's stored flanking sequence/variation (variant_flanking_sequence) against what's computed live from the assembly FASTA and current mutation detail, at the feature's location on whichever assembly ZFIN currently treats as authoritative. Character-level diff highlighting makes a 1-2bp difference inside a 500bp sequence actually visible. No DB writes.
Three sections, because they need different follow-up:
- Drift: stale values (e.g. left by the old GRCz11-hardcoded Flank-Seq batch job after a feature also gained a GRCz12tu location). Fixable, but only by hand -- see below. - Ambiguous location: more than one location row on the current assembly, with different coordinates (sometimes different chromosomes). No single right answer to recompute against -- needs a curator to resolve the duplicate, not a backfill. - Submitter-provided: flanking sequence that came from the Sanger ZMP data submission rather than being computed. Never recomputed by anything; listed so the exclusion is visible.
NOTHING IS FIXED AUTOMATICALLY. This job only reports. Load-Flank-Seq_w is manual-only (ZFIN-10486) and no longer runs nightly, so acting on the Drift section means triggering that job by hand with FORCE_FULL_UPDATE=true, plus INCLUDE_SANGER=true if "sa" features appear in the report. Then re-run this job to confirm the count drops.

email.subject: $PROJECT_DEFAULT_SUBJECT
email.body:
Flanking-sequence drift report attached (Drift / Ambiguous location / Submitter-provided).
This job only reports -- nothing is fixed automatically. To correct what the Drift section lists, trigger Load-Flank-Seq_w by hand with FORCE_FULL_UPDATE=true, adding INCLUDE_SANGER=true if "sa" features appear in the report. That job is manual-only and no longer runs nightly. Re-run this check afterwards to confirm the drift count drops.
The other two sections are not fixable that way: Ambiguous location needs a curator to resolve duplicate location rows, and Submitter-provided is deliberately never recomputed.
